compensating.why: hop 2 decides the side from the sign of d and a comparison with direction
hop 3 restores the sign with Math.copySign
hop 3 takes the magnitude by clearing the sign bit

ownership_reason: Only the gold holds a magnitude together with its gap to the adjacent representable magnitude; hop 1 sees only whether d is zero, hop 2 only the side of the move, hop 3 only the sign, hop 4 passes the pair along. Whether the gap below is the full or half ulp depends on the mantissa bits of the magnitude, which no caller inspects, and once two representable steps have been taken no caller can tell from the returned value that a binade boundary was crossed. The convention is pinned outside the gold: the facade's javadoc ('the smallest machine representable number strictly greater than d is returned; otherwise the largest representable number strictly less than d'); MathUtils.EPSILON = 0x1.0p-53, the smallest positive number such that 1 - EPSILON is not numerically equal to 1, so the number below the power of two 1.0 is half of Math.ulp(1.0) away; MathUtils.scalb moves the exponent field of a double in whole steps of 2^52 in its raw bits; the production caller MathUtils.roundUnscaled takes floor or ceil of nextAfter(unscaled, +-infinity) as the immediate neighbour of the unscaled value (MathUtilsTest testRoundFloat); testNextAfterSpecialCases pins one representable step at both ends of the range (MIN_VALUE -> 0, MAX_VALUE -> infinity), testArrayEquals and testArrayHash that nextAfter(1, 2) is a different number.
